summary: Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at University College London (~1934–1936). He served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from 1945 to 1946.

Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) studied Buddhist and religious studies under Manshi Kiyozawa, Kyoshi Takahama, and Shimei Futabatei at Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He held leadership posts at Shinshu Otani-ha and Higashi Hongan-ji.

Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1967–1970) under D. C. Lau, as well as under Nicole Vandier-Nicolas and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Heeraman Tiwari is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned degrees from Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Heidelberg University, and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Hege Myrlund Larsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bergen under the supervision of Bruce Kapferer (attested 2009).
Hegoda Khemananda is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

Heidi Fjeld is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Oxford and the University of Oslo under Signe Howell, later serving as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Oslo from around 2006 to 2010.
Heidi I. Koppl is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed an MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and studied under the traditional teacher Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi R. M. Pauwels is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Washington under Alan Entwistle. She lectured at SOAS before becoming a professor at the University of Washington in 1996 and 2002.

Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen, Kerala Kalamandalam, and the University of Würzburg. She held academic posts at Tübingen (2005–2008), Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and Sapienza University of Rome (2025).

Heiner Eichner (1942–2024) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1964–1974). He held a post at the University of Vienna from around 1989 to 2010.

Heinrich August Jäschke (1817–1883) was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky in 1847 and as a missionary for the Moravian Church and Moravian Mission in Kyelang between 1856 and 1868.

Heinrich Blochmann (1838–1878) studied at Leipzig, Paris, and Calcutta under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and Karl Benedikt Hase. Active in Indology and Central Asian history, he held posts at Doveton College, The Asiatic Society, and Aliah University.
Heinrich Brunn (1822–1894) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1839–1843) and held a post at the University of Munich from around 1865 to 1894.

Heinrich Ewald (1803–1875) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and Thomas Christian Tychsen, later serving as professor at Göttingen and the University of Tübingen.

Heinrich Gustav Hotho (1802–1873) was a scholar in the field of philosophy. He completed his studies at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1820–1826) and subsequently held an academic post there from approximately 1829 to 1873.

Heinrich Hettrich (1947–2020) was a linguist and Indologist educated at Saarland, Giessen, and Munich. He held posts at Saarland, Munich, and Marburg before becoming Chair of Comparative Linguistics at the University of Würzburg in 1989.

Heinrich Hübschmann (1848–1908) studied linguistics and Iranian studies at Jena, Tübingen, Munich, and Leipzig under August Schleicher and Martin Haug. He held professorships at the University of Leipzig (1876) and the University of Strasbourg (1877).

Heinrich Kiepert (1818–1899) studied under August Boeckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann at Berlin and earned a doctorate at Jena. A geography and archaeology scholar, he held posts at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (1801–1888) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Gottfried Hermann, and Caussin de Perceval. In 1836, he was appointed to the Oriental languages chair at Leipzig.
